deadline.value: Priority review begins March 15, 2027 for Fall 2027 admission (final Fall deadline is April 15, 2027; note the catalog states the program admits very few international students due to federal grant constraints).
deadline.quote: The Department of Biological Sciences Graduate Program Committee will review students' application materials (priority review to commence on March 15)

gre_general.value: GRE General Test is required with a combined percentile score of at least 100 and minimum 25th percentile in each section on the program webpage (30th percentile per section in the 2026-2027 Graduate Catalog and Biology Handbook).
gre_general.quote: GRE scores for the General Test must reflect an overall percentile score of 100, with a minimum percentile score of 25 in each of the three content areas (Verbal Reasoning, Quantitative Reasoning and Analytical Writing).

also.quote: PhD in Neuroscience: a combined percentile score of at least 100, with each section at or above the 30th percentile.

gre_subject.value: Discipline-specific GRE Subject Tests (such as Biology or Psychology) are not considered for admission evaluation.
gre_subject.quote: Discipline-specific GREs (e.g., biology) are not considered for evaluation.

supervisor.value: Committee-based admission; institutionally funded students normally complete three first-semester laboratory rotations before GPC finalizes lab placement (grant-funded students may join a sponsor's lab directly).
supervisor.quote: Students admitted with institutional funding (for example, teaching assistantships) normally complete three short laboratory rotations during the first semester. The Graduate Program Committee (GPC) coordinates placements based on student interests, faculty capacity, and departmental priorities.

funding.value: Nearly all students receive tuition scholarships and research or teaching stipends within their first year, though funding is not guaranteed upon admission and unfunded admission usually requires a faculty sponsor commitment.
funding.quote: Nearly all students receive scholarships or research funding within their first year, making DSU’s neuroscience doctoral program one of the most affordable and supportive in the nation. | The department admits a limited number of students to the PhD program, supporting them with tuition scholarships and research stipends from grants. However, funding is not guaranteed upon admission.

entry_route.value: Requires a bachelor's degree in biology or a related field with a minimum 3.0 overall GPA and foundational science prerequisites.
entry_route.quote: Minimum transcript criteria include a 3.0 overall GPA and a bachelor’s degree in biology or a related field.

notes: Warning from 2026-2027 Graduate Catalog: 'currently the program admits very few international students due to federal funding grant constraints.' Minimum 60 total credits (42 coursework, 18 dissertation).
name: Ph.D. in Neuroscience
